# Lint packs

Each pack is a tested set of lint rules, compiler settings, and CI checks aimed at the mistakes agents make in that stack. Every rule fails with a message that says what to do instead, because that message is what the next agent reads. Each pack has `fixtures/bad` that must fail and `fixtures/good` that must pass, and this repository's CI runs both.

`/setup-faker-kit` picks packs from the stacks it detects and installs them. Existing violations go into a baseline, so only new ones fail. To add a rule for a mistake the pack does not cover, run pstack's `/correct`, which writes the rule in the strongest layer that can hold it.

| Pack | Installed when the repository has | What it enforces |
|---|---|---|
| [agnostic](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/agnostic/README.md) | Every repository | Checks for every repository: a single check entry point, a ratchet that stops patterns from spreading, import boundaries, proof that every encoded rule still fires, no new comments, and complete translations. |
| [kotlin-android](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/kotlin-android/README.md) | `settings.gradle.kts` or `settings.gradle` containing `com.android.application` or `com.android.library` | detekt with type resolution, ktlint, strict Android Lint, and Kotlin warnings as errors, each with a native baseline. |
| [kmp](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/kmp/README.md) | `build.gradle.kts` or `settings.gradle.kts` containing `kotlin("multiplatform")` or `org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform` | Kotlin Multiplatform on top of the kotlin-android pack: keeps platform APIs out of commonMain, requires explicit public API, and turns warnings into errors on every target. |
| [rust](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/rust/README.md) | `Cargo.toml` | Clippy in deny mode for the panics, debug output, and unexplained suppressions agents leave behind, plus rustfmt and cargo-deny. |
| [python](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/python/README.md) | `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg` or `setup.py` or `requirements.txt` | ruff with the rule families that catch agent habits, mypy strict, and import-linter layer contracts. |
| [flutter-dart](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/flutter-dart/README.md) | `pubspec.yaml` | A strict analyzer: strict casts, inference, and raw types; TODO/FIXME/HACK as errors; package imports only; no dynamic calls, print, or discarded futures. Plus feature import boundaries and ARB translation checks through the agnostic pack. |
| [swift-ios](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/swift-ios/README.md) | `Package.swift`, or `*.xcodeproj` or `*.xcworkspace` | SwiftLint in strict mode for force unwraps, casts, and tries; ast-grep rules for print, workaround comments, and DispatchQueue.main.async; Swift 6 language mode with complete concurrency checking and warnings as errors. |

## agnostic

Checks for every repository: a single check entry point, a ratchet that stops patterns from spreading, import boundaries, proof that every encoded rule still fires, no new comments, and complete translations.

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
node scripts/agent-checks/ratchet.mjs check
node scripts/agent-checks/import-boundaries.mjs
node scripts/agent-checks/rule-fixtures.mjs
```

Optional checks, added with `--with <name>`:

- `no-new-comments`: `node scripts/agent-checks/no-new-comments.mjs`
- `locale-keys`: `node scripts/agent-checks/locale-keys.mjs`

Tools:

- node >=18: runs scripts/agent-checks/*.mjs with no dependencies
- lefthook >=1.6 (optional): optional pre-push hook

Existing violations: Add a rule to .agents/ratchet.json for any pattern you want to stop spreading, then run `node scripts/agent-checks/ratchet.mjs update` to record today's counts.

Details and the full rule list: [agnostic README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/agnostic/README.md).

## kotlin-android

detekt with type resolution, ktlint, strict Android Lint, and Kotlin warnings as errors, each with a native baseline.

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
./gradlew detektMain detektTest
ktlint "**/*.kt" "**/*.kts" "!**/build/**"
./gradlew lint
./gradlew test
```

Tools:

- detekt 1.23.8: Kotlin static analysis; the Gradle plugin gives it type resolution
- ktlint 1.5.0: formatting and import rules
- JDK 17: Gradle and detekt

Existing violations: Run ./gradlew detektBaseline to write detekt-baseline.xml, run ./gradlew lint once so Android Lint writes lint-baseline.xml, and run ktlint --baseline=ktlint-baseline.xml. Commit all three; new code must pass without additions to them.

Details and the full rule list: [kotlin-android README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/kotlin-android/README.md).

## kmp

Kotlin Multiplatform on top of the kotlin-android pack: keeps platform APIs out of commonMain, requires explicit public API, and turns warnings into errors on every target.

Requires: [kotlin-android](#kotlin-android).

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
./gradlew detekt
./gradlew allTests
```

Tools:

- detekt 1.23.8: commonMain import rules

Existing violations: Same as the kotlin-android pack: ./gradlew detektBaseline, committed.

Details and the full rule list: [kmp README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/kmp/README.md).

## rust

Clippy in deny mode for the panics, debug output, and unexplained suppressions agents leave behind, plus rustfmt and cargo-deny.

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo deny check
```

Tools:

- rust >=1.81: #[expect] and lint reasons are stable from 1.81
- cargo-deny >=0.16: dependency advisories, licenses, and sources

Existing violations: Clippy has no baseline file. For each file with existing violations, add an inner attribute such as #![expect(clippy::unwrap_used, reason = "faker-kit baseline")] at the top, then add a ratchet rule {"id": "rust-baseline", "pattern": "faker-kit baseline", "files": ["*.rs"]} and run ratchet.mjs update. #[expect] fails once the code is fixed, so baselines remove themselves.

Details and the full rule list: [rust README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/rust/README.md).

## python

ruff with the rule families that catch agent habits, mypy strict, and import-linter layer contracts.

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
ruff format --check .
ruff check .
mypy .
lint-imports
```

Tools:

- ruff >=0.15: lint and format
- mypy >=1.10: strict type checking
- import-linter >=2.0: layer contracts

Existing violations: Run `ruff check --add-noqa .` once to mark existing violations, then ratchet the markers: add {"id": "python-noqa", "pattern": "# noqa", "files": ["*.py"]} to .agents/ratchet.json and run ratchet.mjs update. For mypy, list legacy modules in a [mypy-&lt;module&gt;] section with ignore_errors = True and ratchet the count of those sections the same way.

Details and the full rule list: [python README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/python/README.md).

## flutter-dart

A strict analyzer: strict casts, inference, and raw types; TODO/FIXME/HACK as errors; package imports only; no dynamic calls, print, or discarded futures. Plus feature import boundaries and ARB translation checks through the agnostic pack.

Requires: [agnostic](#agnostic).

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test
flutter analyze --fatal-infos
flutter test
```

Tools:

- flutter >=3.24: flutter analyze and flutter test; pure Dart packages can use dart analyze
- flutter_lints >=5.0: dev dependency the analysis_options include needs

Existing violations: The analyzer has no baseline file. Add `// ignore_for_file: <rule>, faker-kit baseline` at the top of each file with existing violations, then add {"id": "dart-baseline", "pattern": "faker-kit baseline", "files": ["*.dart"]} to .agents/ratchet.json and run ratchet.mjs update.

Details and the full rule list: [flutter-dart README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/flutter-dart/README.md).

## swift-ios

SwiftLint in strict mode for force unwraps, casts, and tries; ast-grep rules for print, workaround comments, and DispatchQueue.main.async; Swift 6 language mode with complete concurrency checking and warnings as errors.

Checks added to `scripts/check.sh`:

```bash
swiftlint lint --strict
npx -y -p @ast-grep/cli ast-grep scan
```

Tools:

- swiftlint 0.65.1: built-in lint rules; on Linux use swiftlint-static from packs/tools.sh
- ast-grep >=0.45: structural Swift rules that work without SourceKit (npx -p @ast-grep/cli ast-grep)
- Xcode or Swift >=6.2: Swift 6 language mode and treatAllWarnings

Existing violations: Run `swiftlint lint --write-baseline .swiftlint-baseline.json` once, commit it, and use `swiftlint lint --strict --baseline .swiftlint-baseline.json` in check. For ast-grep findings, add `// ast-grep-ignore: <rule-id>` with the reason `faker-kit baseline` and ratchet that marker in .agents/ratchet.json.

Details and the full rule list: [swift-ios README](../../plugins/trust-ladder/packs/swift-ios/README.md).
